title: Contouring mitigates voiding at the <mark>lithium</mark>/ceramic electrolyte interface on discharging solid-state batteries
abstract: Published online: 23 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41560-026-02172-w Discharge-induced voids are a major barrier to practical <mark>lithium</mark> metal solid-state batteries. Here the authors show that an egg-box-contoured <mark>lithium</mark>–electrolyte interface increases the voiding threshold by an order of magnitude and enables realistic electric vehicle discharge profiles without polarization.

title: Modeling Current Constriction at the <mark>Lithium</mark> Anode Interface in Solid-State Battery Cells
authors: Marco Neudecker, Christopher Mauersberger and Andreas Jossen
abstract: Contact loss between <mark>lithium</mark> anodes and <mark>solid electrolyte</mark> separators (SES) is a key challenge for solid-state batteries. The resulting current constriction (CCS) causes locally elevated current densities and additional overvoltages, which are critical for <mark>dendrite</mark> formation and for interpreting impedance measurements. This work quantifies these effects with three-dimensional finite element simulations. title: Temperature Dependent Phase Separation in LiFePO 4 ...
abstract: Solid state batteries often operate at elevated temperatures to enhance <mark>ionic conductivity</mark>, yet the impact of these conditions on phase separating electrode materials remains poorly understood. In this paper, the effect of temperature on the LiFePO electrode material is investigated by coupling a CALPHAD thermodynamic database with a chemo-electro-mechanical phase field model that describes the spatial and temporal evolution of the phase separation process.
